correctness.rationale: The repaired minimum-starter theorem follows because a white triangle pair or two white center leaves cannot acquire a first blue vertex. For m>=2 the two support lower bounds are tight via a leaf-to-center force; for m=1 the lower-bound starter stalls and each of the three extra-vertex types works. The triangle with one leaf at each core vertex has three leaf pairs and six nonincident core/leaf pairs that work; a single vertex, two core vertices and an incident pair cannot finish. The frozen ring row F_{2r}(2) is false as an exact realizability statement: for example it includes F_6(2), which the independent algebra rules out. In a finite local triangle-core graph the sole minimal ideal C is the socle and universal, and M is a leaf. The double-annihilator property follows from a perfect finite additive character pairing nontrivial on C. Triangle partners are mutual annihilator ideals, and leaves other than M are self-annihilating. Ideals of different pairs intersect in C and sum to M; comparing their cardinalities via a third triangle ideal in the other pair excludes comparable partners when there are at least two pairs. Incomparable partners cover C, giving M/C of dimension two in either the multiple-pair case or the one-pair incomparable case. Its q+1 lines consist of 2n lines in pairs and m−1 isotropic lines. For m=2 the unique isotropic line forces characteristic two and q=2n; therefore n is a power of two. In particular n=6 would require residue-field order 12. The proof also handles the comparable one-pair graph K3(1), the product of three fields, the two odd-field ranges and all realizations. The corrected table is F_{2^r}(2) for r>=1 plus the r=0 instance K3(2). This correction of the frozen assertion is proved directly, not attributed to an uninspected Yu–Wu theorem. Fresh replay checked all 24 bounded fan profiles and all exceptional pairs, with algebraic table substitutions at five even and nine odd field sizes.

value.rationale: The families are motivated by which triangle-core annihilating-ideal graphs actually arise, not by a hand-picked finite enumeration. The zero forcing number alone cannot determine even the number of optimal starters: the two odd-field families at common residue-field size have equal Z and different minimum support families and counts. The one-leaf case shows a precise stall-and-repair mechanism absent from the multiple-leaf case, and the result supplies all labeled minimizing supports for each realizable graph. The tiny net example is a boundary needed to finish the natural domain, not offered as the sole contribution.
residual_risks: The claim does not provide the full zero forcing polynomial or distinguish two rings realizing the same graph. The correction to admissible parameters alone is not the basis for value.
